findings.description: Hardcoded secret or credential in source code
findings.impact: Credentials exposed in version control or logs
findings.remediation: Move secrets to environment variables. Use os.environ.get('MY_SECRET') or a secrets manager.

findings.description: Hardcoded secret or credential in source code
findings.impact: Credentials exposed in version control or logs
findings.remediation: Move secrets to environment variables. Use os.environ.get('MY_SECRET') or a secrets manager.

findings.description: Potential command injection via shell=True with dynamic input
findings.impact: Attacker-controlled input may execute arbitrary OS commands
findings.remediation: Use shell=False (default) and pass arguments as a list: subprocess.run(['cmd', arg], shell=False). Never pass unsanitised user input to shell commands.

findings.impact: Maliciously crafted data can execute arbitrary code during unpickling
findings.remediation: Never unpickle data from untrusted sources. Use JSON/msgpack for serialisation. For yaml.load, use yaml.safe_load(stream) instead.

findings.code: r = requests.get("https://api.example.com", verify=False)  # S005 — TLS disabled
findings.impact: Disabling TLS verification allows man-in-the-middle attacks
findings.remediation: Remove verify=False. If using a self-signed cert, pass verify='/path/to/ca-bundle.crt' instead.

findings.description: eval() or exec() called with non-literal (potentially dynamic) argument
findings.impact: Dynamic code execution — arbitrary Python can be injected and executed
findings.remediation: Avoid eval()/exec() entirely. Use ast.literal_eval() for safe constant parsing, or restructure logic to remove dynamic execution.
